note: What a model saw in each shot, in its own words. Not a score against a fixed vocabulary -- there was no vocabulary. Written at index time and committed, so the edit path never calls a model.
subject: How much of the film's SUBJECT is in each shot, 0 to 1, authored by the model that looked at them. This replaces a CLIP cosine against 37 fixed phrases whose winner beat the runner-up by about one percent.
roles: What a shot is FOR, which is not the same as what is in it. `hold` marks the ones a film is built toward -- a reveal, an end card -- and a reader must not spend them in a flurry however loud the music is there. `skip` is leader and tail. Absent means ordinary.

made_by.saw: one frame from the middle of each shot
made_by.note: A reading, not a measurement and not a guess. It can be wrong in ways a person can see, which is the point of committing it.

effects.note: Which effects may be used on THIS footage, chosen by the model that measured them against it. The vocabulary is keyed to the moment kind and has never looked at the picture, so a drop got either nothing or a sledgehammer depending on which branch of the table it hit.
effects.why: This is macro product photography on near-white: mean brightness 189 of 255. Light has nowhere to go upward, so bloom is mild and blink -- which darkens -- is enormous: 137 of 255 is most of the way to black and reads as the picture breaking, which is the note this project was given about pointless flashing two days ago. Geometric effects fail the other way: the subject is centred, slow and against a flat field, so whip (0.4) and trails (4.9) are invisible and punch is exactly zero. That leaves freeze and bloom, which are the two that a person would actually notice without being hit.
